text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The U.S.-based Didziuliai family, who now control 49 percent of the shares in the Klaipeda Nafta oil terminal, will not buy any of the new 20 million litas share capital emission. The new shares will be bought by Russian oil concerns LUKoil and Jukos. The total reconstruction of the terminal is estimated at 400 million litas.

- Lithuania expects an IBCA rating before Christmas. Lithuanian financial analysts think that Lithuania can potentially be rated by IBCA at BB+ and that Standard & Poor's rating, expected next year, could be BBB-.
- Vandals wrecked a church in Kaunas on Saturday night. All the pictures and statues of saints in the church were damaged and profaned.
- The Homeland Union, who won 35 seats in the first round of the country's parliamentary elections, strengthened their position in Sunday's run-off.
